'''Vicumpriya Perera''' ([[Sinhala language|Sinhala]]: විකුම්ප්‍රිය පෙරේරා) is a Sri Lankan born mathematician, lyricist, poet and music producer.<ref>{{cite web|title=Digital legacy of Sinhala songs|url=https://archives.sundayobserver.lk/2013/08/04/mon03.asp|publisher=Sunday Observer|access-date=5 December 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Vicumpriya Perera – mathematician, translator and electronic recorder|url=http://www.island.lk/index.php?page_cat=article-details&page=article-details&code_title=86512|publisher=Sunday Island|access-date=2 December 2013}}</ref> He has published three books of Sinhala poetry, ''Mekunu Satahan'' (Sinhala: මැකුනු සටහන්) in 2001,<ref>{{cite web|title=Mekunu Satahan ebook|url=http://www.lankaheritage.com/sinhalabooks/VicumpriyaPerera/|access-date=9 December 2013}}</ref> ''Paa Satahan'' (Sinhala: පා සටහන්) in 2013,<ref>{{cite book|last=Perera|first=Vicumpriya|title=Paa Satahan|year=2013|publisher=Sarasavi Publishers|location=Nugegoda, Sri Lanka|isbn=9789556717921|url=http://www.sarasavi.lk/Book/Pa-Satahan-9556717927}}</ref><ref name="cyberspace">{{cite web|title=A homeland in cyberspace|url=https://archives.sundayobserver.lk/2013/08/11/mon03.asp|publisher=Sunday Observer|access-date=5 December 2017}}</ref> and ''Mawbime Suwandha'' (Sinhala: මව්බිමේ සුවඳ) in 2023.<ref>{{cite web|title=Mawbime Suwandha| date=8 January 2023 |url=https://topnewsasia.lk/?p=12963|access-date= 9 April 2023}}</ref> He has written over 200 songs and has produced eleven Sinhala song albums. He currently works as a mathematics professor in [[Ohio]], US.

==Life and career==

Vicumpriya Perera is originally from [[Wattala]], Sri Lanka. He is a graduate of St. Anthony's College, Wattala and [[Ananda College]], [[Maradana]], Sri Lanka. He received a Bachelor of Science degree in mathematics with first class honors from [[University of Colombo]], [[Sri Lanka]] and continued his graduate studies at [[Indiana University - Purdue University at Indianapolis]]. He obtained a doctorate degree from [[Purdue University]] in [[Pure Mathematics]] with research concentrating on [[operator algebra]]s and [[functional analysis]] in 1993.<ref>{{cite book|last=Perera|first=Vicumpriya|title=Real Valued Spectral Flow in a Type II-[infinity] Factor|year=1993|publisher=Purdue University|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=FIqnYgEACAAJ&q=vicumpriya+perera}}</ref>

Vicumpriya Perera lives in Ohio, US, where he has worked as a mathematics professor at [[Kent State University]] (Trumbull campus) since 1998.<ref>{{cite web|title=Vic Perera|url=https://www.kent.edu/math/vic-perera|access-date=5 December 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Vicumpriya Perera|url=https://www.kent.edu/trumbull/profile/vicumpriya-perera|access-date=6 December 2017}}</ref> He works in [[operator algebra]], which is an area of [[pure mathematics]].

Vicumpriya Perera is a past president of the Ohio Mathematical Association of Two year Colleges (OhioMATYC),<ref>{{cite web|title=OhioMATYC|url=https://www.ohiomatyc.org/|access-date=1 April 2023}}</ref> the Ohio Affiliate organization of the American Mathematical Association of Two Year Colleges ([[AMATYC]]). His term of presidency was from 2021 to 2023. He also serves as the immediate past president of the Colombo University Faculty of Science Alumni Association - North America (CUFSAA),<ref>{{cite web|title=CUFSAA-NA|url=https://www.cufsaa.com/|access-date=30 September 2023}}</ref> since the conclusion of his term as president of the association (2021–2023).

''Siththaruwanani'' included songs from the sinhala classical musical genre (sarala gee). Instrumentalists for this album consisted of Sri Lankan musicians Mahendra Pasquel, Sarath Fernando, Dhananjaya Somasiri, Janaka Bogoda, Susil Amarasinghe, Rohana Dharmakeerthi, Shelton Wijesekera, and Dilusha Ravindranath.<ref name="SithInfo" />

==Other productions==
In 2005, Vicumpriya Perera (along with [[Nalin Jayawardena]], and Jaanaka Wimaladharma) produced a compact disc set, ''Dhammapadaya'' (Sinhala: ධම්මපදය),  under the Lanka Heritage label.<ref name="lankaheritage">{{cite web|title=Dhammapada at Lanka Heritage website|url=http://www.lankaheritage.com/?a=dhammapada|access-date=2 December 2013}}</ref> The set contained four discs, and consisted of  complete the [[Dhammapada]] stanzas in the original [[Pali]] language followed by the [[Sinhala language|Sinhala]] translations chanted by venerable Beruwala Siri Sobhitha Thero of the Sri Lanka Buddhist [[Vihara]] in [[Perth]], Australia.{{efn|[[Dhammapada]] is a widely read Buddhist scripture containing 423 [[pali]] verses spanning into 26 chapters called ''varga''.<ref>[[Max Müller|Müller, F. Max]] (1881). ''[[s:Dhammapada (Muller)|The Dhammapada]]'' ([[Sacred Books of the East]], Vol. X). Oxford University Press.</ref>}} In 2006, this disc set had an English release called ''Dhammapada''.<ref name="lankaheritage" /> This version had the original Dhammapada stanzas (again in Pali) followed by the English translations written and rendered by Dr. [[Gil Fronsdal]],<ref>[[Gil Fronsdal]], and [[Jack Kornfield]] (foreword) (2005). ''The [[Dhammapada]]: A New Translation of the Buddhist Classic with Annotations,'' Boston: Shambhala. {{isbn|1-59030-211-7}}.</ref> director and resident teacher Insight Meditation Center, [[Redwood City]], California, US.

In 2012 Vicumpriya Perera (in collaboration with Nalin Jayawardena) produced a Sinhala [[Audiobook]] called  ''Kulageyin Kulageyata'' (Sinhala: කුලගෙයින් කුලගෙයට) under the Lanka Heritage, LLC. The book was written in 2009 by Bhadraji Mahinda Jayatilaka, who provided most of the voice work . The audiobook has a total length of five compact discs, and was published by Sarasavi Publishers,<ref>{{cite web|title=Sarasavi Prakashakayo|url=http://www.sarasavi.lk/|access-date=2 December 2013}}</ref> [[Nugegoda]], Sri Lanka.
